senses.sense_definition: Relating to or situated in the west; western, especially relating to the Western world.

examples.text: The museum features an extensive collection comparing <w>occidental</w> philosophy with Eastern traditions.
Scholars gathered to examine the profound impact of <w>occidental</w> culture on modern legal systems.

traits.comment: Somewhat formal or dated in modern usage

senses.sense_definition: Describing a gem or precious stone of inferior value or quality.

examples.text: The jeweler quickly identified the stone as an <w>occidental</w> topaz rather than a valuable oriental gem.
Due to its cloudy tint, the gemstone was labeled as <w>occidental</w> and sold at a discount.

traits.comment: Historical trade term for lesser-quality gems

senses.sense_definition: A native or inhabitant of the Western world, or a Western Christian belonging to the Latin rite.

examples.text: Many an <w>occidental</w> living in the region found it difficult to adapt to local customs.
The treaty established formal diplomatic relations between the local empire and visiting <w>occidentals</w>.

traits.comment: Rare or dated in general speech

senses.sense_definition: An international auxiliary language created by Edgar de Wahl, later renamed Interlingue.

examples.text: Before it was renamed Interlingue, the planned language was known primarily as <w>Occidental</w>.
He spent years translating classical literary works into <w>Occidental</w> to test its expressiveness.

senses.sense_definition: A census-designated place in Sonoma County, California, United States.

examples.text: We stopped for lunch in <w>Occidental</w> during our weekend drive through Sonoma County.
The historic downtown area of <w>Occidental</w> attracts many tourists visiting California's wine country.
